brandMix.title: Revenue by brand
brandMix.content:
IFBH sells coconut water and related beverages under two brands: if, the core growth brand, and Innococo, a secondary brand distributed through different channels.

For IFBH Limited: Innococo revenue collapsed from US$26.2m in FY2024 to US$1.7m in H1 FY2026 -- a deliberate channel restructuring away from lower-margin or lower-control distribution, not a one-off. The "if" brand kept growing through the same period (US$131.3m to US$166.7m FY2024-FY2025), so the group total understates how concentrated growth now is in a single brand.

What to watch:

  • Whether Innococo stabilises at a smaller base or keeps shrinking toward zero
  • Whether "if" growth alone can offset the Innococo decline going forward
  • Any disclosed reason for the restructuring (margin, distributor dispute, strategy) in the filings

geoMix.title: Revenue by geography
geoMix.content:
Revenue split between Mainland China, Hong Kong, and all markets outside Mainland China (Hong Kong plus other export markets).

For IFBH Limited: Mainland China is roughly 90% of group revenue (US$159.4m of US$176.4m in FY2025), so the business is effectively a single-country bet layered on top of the single-distributor and single-brand risks visible elsewhere on this page. The DCF's WACC was raised in part for this China geographic/regulatory concentration -- see the valuation note above.

What to watch:

  • Any shift in the non-China share, which would reduce single-market dependence
  • Chinese regulatory or import/customs changes affecting imported beverage brands
  • Only disclosed annually -- no interim geographic split exists to show intra-year movement

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For IFBH Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For IFBH Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For IFBH Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For IFBH Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For IFBH Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For IFBH Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For IFBH Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For IFBH Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For IFBH Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For IFBH Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: The multiples sanity check tripped on a thin and misleading historical comparison: only 17 monthly closes exist since the June 2025 IPO, the stock has fallen monotonically from HK$36.60 to HK$4.23, and the single FY2025 historical multiple (P/B 192x, EV/EBITDA 1226x) is an IPO-peak data point on a tiny pre-IPO equity base — not a market-set ceiling. The underlying diagnosis was nonetheless applied in full: WACC was raised 11.0% → 14.2% across all three scenarios to price in real structural risks — small-cap illiquidity (+2.0%), single-distributor concentration (+1.5%, largest customer 50.9% of FY2025 sales), and China geographic/regulatory concentration (+1.5%). The key framing: at HK$4.23 the market cap (≈US$143m) sits below net cash (≈US$161m), so the market is pricing the operating business (the “if” and Innococo coconut-water brands) below zero even after the higher discount rate. This is a net-cash / special-situation thesis, not a growth-multiple bet — though the Innococo channel collapse and ~90% China revenue concentration shown below are real, ongoing risks to monitor, not resolved by the WACC adjustment.
